info.title: golang-vibe-starter API
info.description:
A small HTTP API over a placeholder `items` resource. Item data comes from an upstream service, so a failure to reach or understand the upstream is reported as 502 or 504, never as a 500. Every response carries a `Client-Correlation-Id` header; send one to tie the service's log lines to your own, or quote the one returned when reporting a problem. Every response also carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Cache-Control: no-store`. Every route but `/healthz` needs an API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`): 401 without a valid one, 403 for a write with a read-only key, or a request the request-validation service refuses (where there is one: VALIDATOR_URL). Every request's headers are screened first: a request with a body must send `Content-Type: application/json` (415 otherwise), headers have size limits (431), some may appear only once (400), and proxy and method-override headers (`X-Forwarded-*`, `Forwarded`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-HTTP-Method-Override`) are ignored. A request no route below takes gets a JSON error too: 404, `not_found`, for a path none has; 405, `method_not_allowed`, with `Allow`, for a method its path has no route for; and 400, `invalid_target`, for a target that isn't a path, such as `OPTIONS *`.

This file is checked against the running handlers by tests (`cmd/api/openapi_test.go`): routes, status codes, response bodies, headers and the limits stated here must match what the service actually does.

get.description: Reports ok whenever the process can serve HTTP. It doesn't check the upstream.

Whether to send this instance traffic: 200 while it can reach the upstream (any answer from it counts, an error included), 503 once it is shutting down or if it can't reach the upstream at all. Liveness is /healthz. The result is cached for a second, so frequent probes cost little.

503.description: Not ready: shutting down, or the upstream can't be reached.

get.description: Returns a page of the items, oldest first: up to `limit` (50 without it, at most 200), after `cursor`. When there are more, the response carries `next_cursor`: send it back as `cursor` for the next page; the last page has none. Pages stay right while items are added or deleted: none is skipped or listed twice. A `limit` out of range, or a cursor this list didn't give out, is a 400, `invalid_parameter`. When the `items-list-total` feature flag is on, the response also carries `total`, the number of items on this page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items the page may hold: 1 to 200. Without it, 50.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where the page starts: a `next_cursor` this list gave out. Without it, the start of the list. Opaque: don't make one, or read one.

201.description: The created item, with its URL in `Location`.

get.description: The item, with its `ETag`. Send that as `If-None-Match` to get a 304, with no body, while the item is unchanged; or as `If-Match` on a write, so it can't overwrite a change you haven't seen.

304.description: The item is unchanged since the ETag in If-None-Match. No body.

put.summary: Replace an item's name and description
put.description: With `If-Match`, only if the item is still the version you last saw: otherwise a 412, `precondition_failed`, and nothing changes.

delete.description: With `If-Match`, only if the item is still the version you last saw: otherwise a 412, `precondition_failed`.

204.description: The item was deleted. No body.

apiKey.description: An API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A key may read, or read and write; a read-only key's writes get 403. `make api-key` generates one. A deployment can leave reads open (API_AUTH_READS=open), or, for local development only, turn authentication off (API_AUTH=off).

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: Write only if the item is still this version: an `ETag` from a read or a write, several separated by commas, or `*` for any version, as long as the item exists. A weak tag (`W/...`) never matches. Without it, the write goes ahead whatever the version.

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: An `ETag` you hold (or `*`): if the item still has it, the answer is a 304 with no body.

APIVersion.name: API-Version
APIVersion.description: The API version the request is written for. Without it, the current one. A version the API doesn't serve is a 400, `unsupported_api_version`; the probes accept any. Versioning is by this header, never by path.

ItemID.name: id
ItemID.description: The item's ID: 1 to 128 letters, digits, `-` and `_`. No item has any other ID, so any other value is answered with 404.

CorrelationID.name: Client-Correlation-Id
CorrelationID.description: Your own ID for this request. It is echoed in the response and appears as `request_id` on every log line for the request. A value that doesn't fit the schema is ignored, and the service generates one instead.

ETag.description: The item's version: it changes whenever the item does. Quoted, as HTTP's entity tags are.

APIVersion.description: The API version that answered: the one asked for in the API-Version request header, or the current one without it.

CorrelationID.description: The request's correlation ID: yours if you sent a valid one, otherwise one the service generated.

ItemInput.description: The body of a create or replace. The body is limited to 1 MiB, and fields other than these are rejected.

name.description: Required. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and what's left must be 1 to 200 characters.

next_cursor.description: Where the next page starts: send it as `cursor`. Absent on the last page.

total.description: The number of items on this page. Present only when the `items-list-total` feature flag is on.

error.description: A short message safe to show a client. Details are logged, not returned. Written for people, and may be reworded: act on `code`.

code.description: What the error means, for a client to act on: stable, unlike `error`. Two errors with one status can mean different things (a 403 for a read-only key, or one the validation service refused), and the code tells them apart.

PreconditionFailed.description: The item isn't the version `If-Match` names: it changed since you read it (or, for `*`, it doesn't exist). Nothing was changed: get it again, and retry with its new `ETag`.

BadRequest.description: The body isn't usable (malformed JSON, the wrong shape or types, an unknown field, an empty body, or over 1 MiB), a header that may appear only once (Content-Type, Authorization, Client-Correlation-Id, API-Version) appears more than once, an API-Version the API doesn't serve (`unsupported_api_version`), or a query parameter that isn't valid: a list's `limit` out of range, or a `cursor` it didn't give out (`invalid_parameter`).

DuplicateHeader.description: A header that may appear only once (Content-Type, Authorization, Client-Correlation-Id, API-Version) appears more than once.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request has a body, but not Content-Type: application/json (parameters such as charset are fine).

Unauthorized.description: No API key, or not a valid one. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

Forbidden.description: The API key may only read, and this is a write; or, where the service checks requests (VALIDATOR_URL), the request-validation service refused the request. The reason is logged, not sent.

TooManyRequests.description: Over the client's rate limit: by default 100 requests a second on average, in bursts of up to 200 (RATE_LIMIT, RATE_BURST). A client is its API key, or its IP address without one (an IPv6 client is its /64). Retry after the given number of seconds.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The service is serving as many requests as it takes at once (MAX_IN_FLIGHT, 512 by default), or, where the service checks requests (VALIDATOR_URL) and fails closed, the request-validation service can't answer, or the service is shutting down and stopped the request (`shutting_down`). Retry after the given number of seconds.

HeadersTooLarge.description: The request's headers are over a limit. By default: more than 100 headers, more than 8 KiB for any one header (name and value), or more than 32 KiB in total; a deployment can change these (HEADER_MAX_COUNT, HEADER_MAX_BYTES, HEADER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES).

Unprocessable.description: The body is well-formed but a value is invalid: `name` is missing, blank, or too long.

InternalError.description: An unexpected failure in this service itself.

BadGateway.description: The upstream couldn't give a usable answer: connection refused or reset, an error status, a body that wouldn't decode, or an item that breaks the API's own rules (an ID, name or description it couldn't have made).

GatewayTimeout.description: The upstream didn't answer in time: within `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, or before the request reached its deadline, `REQUEST_TIMEOUT`.
